blocks.text:
This was Alexandra's favorite park
in all of Grass Valley.
Alexandra ran in, ready to play.

Swings. Tunnels. Sand.
A climbing wall like a mountain.

The slide looked even longer
from here.

Alexandra did not
know what to do.

pages.notes: some text on this page may need a very subtle/blurred shadow to distinguish it from the background.

blocks.text:
That night, Alexandra 
sat quietly on the bed.
The big feeling  was still there.
"That was scary," said a tiny voice.
A light blinked  beside the bed.

The lights made a path
across the floor.

"Let's look together,"
said the tiny voice.
"This way," said the voice. "Whenever you're ready."
On the quiet path  lay a clue:

Before Alexandra could peek,
voices called from every direction.

"This way!" blinked a star.
"No, this way!" puffed the wind.

pages.notes: everything except "and there it was: a tiny path" needs to be on the previous page, lower half.

blocks.text:
"Too many voices make it
hard to hear your own,"

Alexandra listened for
the small, true voice inside.

And there it was:
a quiet path.

pages.notes: this page may also need a subtle/blurry shadow behind the text

blocks.text:
One way was smooth and shiny.
It looked easy.
The other was plain and steep.
Alexandra looked at the shiny path. It was pretty.
At the top, a cave glittered.

pages.notes:
to reduce text on this page, maybe we make a change similar to this:

"YOU CANT'T! YOU'RE TOO LITTLE!"
The tiny voice echoed throughout the cave, and the same words glowed on a wall in big prickly letters.

blocks.text: Alexandra felt scared. Alexandra's tummy felt tight.
The tiny voice echoed through the cave.
The same words glowed on it in big, prickly letters.
The tiny voice didn't sound friendly now.

"Why do you sound mean?" 
asked Alexandra.

pages.notes:
the following need to be moved to the next page:

"The prickly words wiggled. Then softened."

blocks.text: The voice was quiet. Alexandra remembered.

pages.notes: We can remove "The words opened." and "I'M A LITTLE SCARED. THIS FEELS TOO BIG." (since it's on the wall and we use a colon after "inside were smaller words"

blocks.text: The words opened. Inside were smaller words:
I'M A LITTLE SCARED.  THIS FEELS TOO BIG.
"Oh. You weren't trying to be mean."
The tiny voice felt warm again.

pages.notes: This page feels a little awkward. Not sure what to do about it.

blocks.text: "Sometimes big feelings come out sharp," said the voice.

"But if you listen close, you can hear what they
are really trying to say."

The prickles fell away.
The wall shimmered.
Beyond it, the world was bright.

blocks.text: "I want to see you," said Alexandra.
A trail of feathers glowed ahead.
The forest grew warmer and quieter.

"Listen close," said the tiny voice.
"That quiet is your heart."

blocks.text: In a warm, magical clearing, Owl appeared.
"I am your quiet voice," said Owl, "in a shape you can see."
The warm quiet was inside Alexandra, too.
The magical forest grew small below.

Ahead was the park, the ladder,
and the very, very tall slide.

Owl stayed close.
So did the quiet voice.
Alexandra was back at the top.
This time, Alexandra  knew what to do.

blocks.text: The quiet voice was there. Small and warm.
Alexandra looked at the child waiting behind them.
Trace the spiral with your finger.

Breathe in as you go around.
Breathe out as you come back.
Think of something you'd like to try.
How does it make you feel?

Listen close. Does your quiet voice say
"no," "not yet," or "yes"?
